warnings.message: Topic has no hard prerequisites and is not marked foundational.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Joint frequency cell
node.description: Interpret an interior cell in a two-way table as the count satisfying both row and column attributes.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Marginal totals in two-way tables
node.description: Use row totals and column totals in a two-way table as marginal totals for single attributes.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Grand total as denominator
node.description: Use the grand total as the denominator when finding probabilities over the whole two-way table population.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Row or column denominator selection
node.description: Choose a row total, column total or grand total as denominator based on the event condition being asked.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Table probability from counts
node.description: Convert counts in a two-way table into probabilities using the appropriate denominator.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Venn overlap region
node.description: Interpret the overlap of two event circles in a Venn diagram as outcomes satisfying both events.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Venn outside region
node.description: Interpret the region outside all event circles as outcomes satisfying none of the shown events.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Disjoint events from a diagram
node.description: Recognise from a Venn diagram or table when two events have no overlap.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Overlap subtraction in a union
node.description: Subtract the overlap once when finding the probability or count of a union of overlapping events.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Mutually exclusive addition rule
node.description: Add probabilities directly for mutually exclusive events because no outcomes are shared.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Non-mutually exclusive addition rule
node.description: Use the adjusted addition rule for events that can occur together by subtracting their intersection.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Translate words to union and intersection
node.description: Translate everyday compound event wording into union, intersection and complement relationships.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: De Morgan language introduction
node.description: Interpret simple not-and and not-or compound event statements using Venn diagram regions.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Tree path outcome
node.description: Read a complete path through a tree diagram as one ordered compound outcome.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Path probability product
node.description: Find the probability of a complete path in a tree diagram by multiplying branch probabilities along that path.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Sum paths for an event
node.description: Add probabilities of separate tree-diagram paths that satisfy the same event.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Ordered outcomes in sequential events
node.description: Recognise that order may matter in sequential probability outcomes such as heads then tails versus tails then heads.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Replacement updates the sample space
node.description: Track whether items are replaced after each draw to decide whether later sample spaces and probabilities change.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Branch probability after previous outcome
node.description: Update branch probabilities in a dependent tree diagram based on the previous outcome.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Choose table Venn or tree representation
node.description: Choose an appropriate representation for a compound-event problem based on whether it involves attributes, overlaps or sequential stages.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Joint cell means both attributes
node.description: An interior two-way table cell counts outcomes satisfying both the row attribute and the column attribute.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Union overlap is subtracted once
node.description: For overlapping events, adding both event totals counts the overlap twice, so the overlap must be subtracted once.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Tree path probabilities multiply
node.description: The probability of a full tree-diagram path is the product of the branch probabilities along that path.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Separate paths add for an event
node.description: Separate non-overlapping tree paths that satisfy the same event have probabilities that are added.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Table denominator always grand total
node.description: Learner always uses the grand total as denominator even when the question conditions on a row or column group.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Tree path branches added instead of multiplied
node.description: Learner adds branch probabilities along a single tree path instead of multiplying them.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Order ignored in sequential outcomes
node.description: Learner treats different ordered paths as the same outcome when order matters in a sequential chance process.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Without replacement keeps same denominator
node.description: Learner fails to update the sample space after an item is drawn without replacement.

edge.rationale: Interpreting joint cells is core practice for reading two-way table structure.
The overlap region is central to interpreting Venn diagrams for compound events.
Subtracting overlap is direct practice for the addition rule with overlapping events.
Finding path probabilities is core tree-diagram outcome practice.
Choosing between table, Venn and tree representations supports compound-event representation fluency.
Joint-cell interpretation depends on knowing row and column structure.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reads an interior cell as a row total or column total.

edge.rationale: Marginal totals are interpreted after distinguishing interior joint cells from totals.
edge.failure_signal: Learner confuses marginal totals with joint frequencies.

edge.rationale: The grand total is understood through row and column totals in the table structure.
edge.failure_signal: Learner uses a marginal total as the whole-population denominator without checking the condition.

edge.rationale: Selecting a denominator requires distinguishing whole-table and subgroup totals.
edge.failure_signal: Learner always uses the grand total regardless of the condition in the question.

edge.rationale: Converting counts into probabilities requires choosing the appropriate denominator.
edge.failure_signal: Learner forms a correct count but divides by the wrong total.

edge.rationale: The overlap region is one part of interpreting Venn regions.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reads the overlap as union rather than intersection.

edge.rationale: The outside region requires recognising the universal set and event circles.
edge.failure_signal: Learner ignores outcomes outside the drawn circles.

edge.rationale: Recognising disjoint events depends on seeing whether an overlap region exists.
edge.failure_signal: Learner assumes any two named events can overlap or cannot overlap without checking the diagram.

edge.rationale: Overlap subtraction depends on distinguishing union from intersection.
edge.failure_signal: Learner double-counts outcomes in both events.

edge.rationale: Direct addition applies when events are disjoint and have no overlap.
edge.failure_signal: Learner adds probabilities directly even when events overlap.

edge.rationale: The non-mutually-exclusive addition rule uses overlap subtraction.
edge.failure_signal: Learner forgets to subtract the intersection after adding event probabilities.

edge.rationale: Translation from words to event operations depends on understanding and/or event language.
edge.failure_signal: Learner maps 'or' to intersection or treats 'and' as union.

edge.rationale: Introductory not-and/not-or reasoning uses complement regions but is an extension beyond basic complement work.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot shade or describe the complement of a compound event.

edge.rationale: Reading a complete path depends on interpreting tree outcomes.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats one branch as a full outcome instead of the full path.

edge.rationale: Path probability calculation depends on identifying the complete path outcome first.
edge.failure_signal: Learner adds branch probabilities instead of multiplying along the path.

edge.rationale: Adding paths for an event requires first calculating each path probability.
edge.failure_signal: Learner multiplies probabilities across alternative paths instead of adding them.

edge.rationale: Order matters in many sequential event sample spaces.
edge.failure_signal: Learner combines distinct ordered outcomes when the sequence matters.

edge.rationale: Updating the sample space is central to without-replacement contexts.
edge.failure_signal: Learner keeps the same denominator after drawing an item without replacement.

edge.rationale: Dependent branch probabilities often change after previous outcomes alter the sample space.
edge.failure_signal: Learner copies first-branch probabilities to every later branch in a dependent context.

edge.rationale: Choosing a representation depends on understanding the structure of the compound-event wording.
edge.failure_signal: Learner uses a tree for a non-sequential overlap problem or a Venn diagram for a staged process without justification.
